pages.title: Why bundles
pages.text: Grain crops drop a grain bundle instead of loose grain. The bundle is threshed with a knife to recover grain and wet grass.

pages.title: Wet grass
pages.text: Wet grass is a B item. Dry it on a drying rack or another supported drying recipe to obtain straw.

pages.title: Grain list
pages.text: Bundles exist for ten A grains (millet, foxtail millet, fonio, spelt, emmer, einkorn, pearl millet, finger millet, sorghum, Job's tears) and six TFC grains (barley, oat, rice, rye, wheat, maize).

pages.title: Uses
pages.text: Grain keeps its normal food and recipe uses. Wet grass is accepted by medium compost greens. Bundles themselves are crafting intermediates, not food.

pages.title: Grain bundle
pages.text: The bundle is the intermediate drop. Thresh it with a knife for grain and wet grass.

pages.title: Wet grass
pages.text: Dry wet grass to obtain straw; it is also a medium compost green.
